findings.highlight: Fuji-nee and Sakura would have made fun of Saber to make her angry
findings.evidenceJa: 桜と藤ねえにいびられたセイバーは怒っているだろうし
findings.governingReading: In Shirou’s worst-case scenario, Saber may be angry after being bullied, harried, or picked on by Sakura and Taiga.
findings.explanation: The English weakens いびられた to “made fun of” and adds the unsupported purpose “to make her angry,” turning a feared consequence into their intention.

findings.highlight: Sakura’s pretty stubborn too.
findings.evidenceJa: 桜だってアレで機嫌を損ねると中々に手強い。
findings.governingReading: For all her usual gentleness, Sakura becomes quite formidable when her mood is soured.
findings.explanation: “Pretty stubborn” converts a conditional, rarely seen response to offense into a standing personality trait, changing Shirou’s knowledge of her anger.

findings.highlight: Fuji-nee, since she’s the one who’ll be over it if they did have a fight last night
findings.evidenceJa: 昨夜大喧嘩があったとしても朝にはケロッと忘れている藤ねえ
findings.governingReading: Taiga would have completely and cheerfully forgotten even a huge fight by morning.
findings.explanation: The English omits both the fixed morning recovery and ケロッと’s striking total lack of lingering concern, weakening why she is the ideal witness.

findings.highlight: I slide open the shouji. And I step into the tiger’s den.
findings.evidenceJa: ガラッ、と勢いよく障子を開ける。んで、気合をいれて虎口に踏み込んで
findings.governingReading: Shirou violently slides the shouji open, steels himself, and steps into the tiger’s jaws.
findings.explanation: The English removes the speed and force of the door action and his act of psyching himself up, flattening the mock-battle escalation before Taiga throws him out.

findings.highlight: grabbing me, rolling three times, and throwing me
findings.evidenceJa: 襟首を掴んでごろんごろんと三回転したあげく放り投げた地獄車
findings.governingReading: Taiga grabbed Shirou by the collar, rolled him through three rotations, and finished by hurling him with a “Hell Wheel” wrestling-style throw.
findings.explanation: The English omits the collar grip and named Hell Wheel technique, reducing a specific absurd grappling sequence to generic rolling and throwing.

findings.highlight: at least help me up.
findings.evidenceJa: 手を貸せこの大トラ
findings.governingReading: Shirou demands help from “this great tiger,” a direct punning insult built on Taiga’s name and ferocity.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the form of address entirely, losing the punch line of his angry demand and their familiar combative register.

findings.highlight: doing a special attack against this super robot that came to invade Earth.
findings.evidenceJa: 侵略専用最強ロボ相手にロメロスペシャルを決めた手ごたえが？
findings.governingReading: Taiga recalls the tactile satisfaction of landing a Romero Special wrestling hold on the strongest robot purpose-built for invasion.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the named hold with “a special attack,” adds Earth, and collapses the robot’s absurd design specification into merely having come to invade.

findings.highlight: The question marks appearing beside her make me think that she might recall the event, but she probably won’t.
findings.evidenceJa: ぴょこぴょこ点滅するハテナマークが、たった数分前の記憶を呼び起こしそうで呼び起こさない。
findings.governingReading: Bobbing, blinking question marks almost—but do not—revive Taiga’s memory from only minutes ago.
findings.explanation: The English removes the animated blinking/bobbing and converts the comic definite near-recall into Shirou’s probability guess, weakening both visual presentation and timing.

findings.highlight: That’s a big lie.
findings.evidenceJa: 嘘虚言紛らわしい。
findings.governingReading: Shirou fires back with an emphatic, redundant “lies, falsehoods—misleading,” exploiting the written/ruby layers for mock-official denial.
findings.explanation: “A big lie” preserves accusation but removes the layered synonym joke and misleading-label complaint about Taiga counting herself as a girl.

findings.highlight: we were at least ten feet apart
findings.evidenceJa: 十歩ぐらい間合いが離れてた
findings.governingReading: Shirou and Taiga had roughly ten paces of fighting distance between them.
findings.explanation: The English changes 歩 from paces or steps to feet and adds “at least,” substantially shortening and falsely hardening the distance that makes her instant strike absurd.

findings.highlight: You’re pretty kind, Shirou.
findings.evidenceJa: 士郎にしてはちゃんと気が利くじゃない。
findings.governingReading: Taiga remarks that, for Shirou, he is surprisingly perceptive and properly considerate this time.
findings.explanation: “Pretty kind” drops 士郎にしては’s teasingly low expectation and 気が利く’s situational perceptiveness, turning a barbed compliment into plain praise.

findings.highlight: I can endure it.
findings.evidenceJa: 我慢するしかないコトだ。
findings.governingReading: If Sakura dislikes him, Shirou believes he has no choice but to endure it.
findings.explanation: “I can endure it” makes tolerance a confident capability rather than an unavoidable consequence he reluctantly accepts.

findings.highlight: I don’t like it if Saber and Sakura feel bad.
findings.evidenceJa: 桜とセイバーがイヤな思いをするのは、なんか損してると思うし
findings.governingReading: Shirou thinks it would be a needless loss or waste for Sakura and Saber both to have an unpleasant experience.
findings.explanation: “I don’t like it” replaces his characteristic judgment that mutual unhappiness costs them something with generic personal preference.

findings.highlight: Saber-chan’s kind don’t get along with her kind.
findings.evidenceJa: 桜ちゃんはセイバーちゃんみたいな子が苦手だから
findings.governingReading: Sakura has difficulty with people like Saber, so she has not yet grown accustomed to her.
findings.explanation: The English mutualizes Sakura’s one-sided discomfort, turns both girls into opposing “kinds,” and suggests inherent incompatibility rather than a personal adjustment still underway.

findings.highlight: they’ve made peace
findings.evidenceJa: 二人とも和解したようだし
findings.governingReading: It appears that the two have reconciled.
findings.explanation: The English removes ようだ, presenting Taiga’s outside impression as established fact despite Sakura’s and Saber’s stated residual discomfort.

findings.highlight: the problem here is solved now.
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮家の問題はなんとか解決してくれたようだから
findings.governingReading: Shirou is glad because Taiga appears somehow to have managed to resolve the Emiya-household problem for him.
findings.explanation: The English removes Taiga’s credited intervention, なんとか’s qualified success, and よう’s tentative observation, replacing them with categorical resolution.

findings.highlight: Fuji-nee left her student lying on the ground
findings.evidenceJa: 倒れた弟分を最後まで放置していきやがった
findings.governingReading: Taiga abandons to the end the fallen younger-brother figure or junior she claims as family.
findings.explanation: “Student” replaces 弟分’s intimate quasi-sibling/junior relationship with an institutional teacher-pupil relation, weakening Shirou’s complaint about familial neglect.

findings.highlight: I can’t stand up after hitting the ground so hard
findings.evidenceJa: 激しく腰を打って立ち上がれない俺
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot stand because he struck his lower back or hips violently in the throw.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes the specific injured body area into the ground impact itself, obscuring why he physically cannot rise.

findings.highlight: And I’m flung outside.
findings.evidenceJa: ものの見事に、場外に投げ飛ばされた。
findings.governingReading: He is spectacularly hurled out of bounds or outside the ring.
findings.explanation: The English drops ものの見事に (“magnificently/spectacularly”) and 場外 (“out of bounds/out of the ring”), flattening a deliberately staged comic defeat into a generic fall.

findings.highlight: Dismissing what happened with a mere “oh well” is inexcusable.
findings.evidenceJa: まいっか、などでさっきの三回転を帳消しにされては堪らない。
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot stand Fuji erasing the three rotations from moments ago with a casual “oh well.”
findings.explanation: The English generalizes さっきの三回転 (“those three rotations just now”) to “what happened,” losing the exact comic callback and physical grievance.

findings.highlight: As expected from a black belt. I keep forgetting, but Fuji-nee was a well-known swordsman back in her student days.
findings.evidenceJa: さすが有段者、時々忘れるけど藤ねえは学生時代名を馳せた剣士なのだった。
findings.governingReading: As expected of someone with a formal dan rank, Fuji was a swordswoman who made a name for herself during her student days.
findings.explanation: “Black belt” is an imprecise Western martial-arts equivalent for 有段者, and “swordsman” uses a male-coded term for Fuji while weakening the specific “made a name” history.
